title: First after Op Sindoor: India invites Pak to SCO meeting in Delhi
syllabus: GS2 › India and its neighbourhood – relations; Important international institutions, agencies and fora (SCO)
summary: India has invited Pakistan's culture minister to the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi (20–21 November), the first invite to a senior Pakistani minister since Operation Sindoor.
ideas: Bilateral freeze, multilateral engagement: India keeps direct ties with Pakistan frozen over terror, but meets it on platforms like the SCO, where hosting obliges it to invite every member.
GS2 answers on India–Pakistan relations: shows engagement without a 'thaw'.
Civilisational diplomacy: the forum aims at people-to-people ties and the shared heritage, art and literature of Eurasia, a soft-power track when politics is stuck.
GS2 answers on soft power and cultural exchange (see 2015 question below).
The SCO is India's channel to raise connectivity, regional connectivity, transit and trade with Pakistan and Central Asia; Pakistan hosts the next SCO summit, so engagement will continue.
GS2 answers on regional groupings and India's Central Asia outreach.
keywords: SCO meet on culture and heritage, proposed by PM Modi at Tianjin (2025); New Delhi hosts it on 20–21 Nov 2026
Example of India shaping the SCO agenda.
No direct talks with Pakistan, but contact at multilateral forums
The terror attacks and military response that froze ties
Background line in any India–Pakistan answer.
Issues an Indian official flagged at the SCO national coordinators' meeting in Islamabad
Common ground India and Pakistan could work on.
'Eurasian and Asian landmass … together on the SCO platform'
Description of the SCO by Alok Dimri, India's SCO national coordinator
Quotable line on the SCO's reach.
Using shared culture and heritage to build goodwill
examples: Pakistan's then Foreign Minister attended the SCO Foreign Ministers' meeting, the last senior Pakistani visit to India
Multilateral channel working despite frozen ties.
EAM attended the SCO Council of Heads of Government meeting and met senior Pakistani leaders in the SCO format
The same channel used in the other direction.
evolution: Pathankot and Uri attacks; India freezes bilateral ties with Pakistan.
Ties downgraded further; both countries recall their envoys.

An Indian delegation attends the SCO national coordinators' meeting in Islamabad, the first Indian presence at an SCO meeting in Pakistan in almost two years.

Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi; Pakistan's minister invited.
pyqs: Directly usable: the civilisational dialogue is soft power at work, with a cultural forum inviting Pakistan even while political ties stay frozen.
India's role: using the SCO to keep dialogue open (hosting the forum, inviting Pakistan) while raising connectivity, transit and trade.
Importance for India: a platform to engage Pakistan and Central Asia that bilateral channels do not offer.
The forum showcases shared Eurasian heritage and India's outreach to SCO's Central Asian members.

title: China says it is strictly abiding by pacts with India amid LAC face-offs in Arunachal
syllabus: GS2 › India and its neighbourhood · GS3 › Security challenges in border areas
context: Days after the ITBP chief spoke of face-offs at several locations in Arunachal Pradesh, China said it strictly abides by agreements and conducts normal patrols. India's MEA said friction occurs when Chinese forces depart from established patrolling patterns in border pockets.
ideas: Normalisation since Galwan is real but fragile: friction on the ground keeps returning.
Dialogue at many levels (Corps Commander, diplomatic, leaders) keeps small incidents from escalating.
keywords: The three stages of easing a military stand-off
Shows precise understanding of LAC talks.
Steps that reduce the risk of miscalculation
examples: Deadly clash followed by a stand-off of over four years
Reference point for the state of India-China ties.
pyqs: Recurring face-offs in Arunachal show why border infrastructure and the ITBP's role on the China border matter.
Border management needs mechanisms like Corps Commander talks to avoid 'misunderstanding and miscalculation'.
summary: Fresh face-offs in Arunachal Pradesh: China says it follows the border pacts; India says friction comes when Chinese patrols depart from agreed patterns.
evolution: Deadly Galwan clashes, followed by a military face-off that lasted over four years.
Last two years
Both sides took measures to rebuild relations.
Corps Commander talks at the Wacha-Damai border meeting point.

Modi and Xi met at the BRICS summit in New Delhi; Modi stressed the 'three mutuals'.

Fresh face-offs reported in Arunachal.

title: Climate justice needs quicker compensation: first Loss and Damage payout to Nepal
syllabus: GS3 › Environment; Disaster management · GS2 › International institutions; India's neighbourhood · GS4 › Ethical issues in international funding
context: The UN's Fund for Loss and Damage has allocated $21.6 million (about Rs 190 crore) to Nepal, nearly two months after devastating floods. It is the first time the Fund has earmarked a grant for a disaster-affected nation. The Indian Express argues the episode should become a case study for reforming the Fund.
ideas: Loss and damage is compensation, not charity, because it rests on responsibility for climate change.
GS3 climate answers; GS2 global governance.
Speed is justice: delays raise hardship and rebuilding costs, especially for poor countries.
Money is short: $822 million pledged, about a third of pending claims.
keywords: Climate harm beyond what mitigation and adaptation can prevent
Sharing climate burdens by responsibility and capacity
Common but differentiated responsibilities and respective capabilities
Those who cause harm bear its cost
data: Low emitter, high loss: the equity argument.
Pledged to the Fund, about a third of pending claims
examples: Barely 0.1% of emissions, yet among the hardest hit
An ice-and-rock avalanche set off flash floods and wrecked hydropower plants
Cascading Himalayan hazards in disaster answers.
pyqs: Loss-and-damage finance as part of climate commitments: first grant, $822 million pledged against far larger claims.
Nepal's avalanche-triggered floods as a Himalayan climate hazard with cross-border lessons.
Nepal lost at least 10% of its hydropower facilities: infrastructure in fragile terrain.
Nepal's case shows who pays for 'development' driven by greed: low emitters, high losses.
links: Related Explained (Telegram): Why Rs 190 crore payout to Nepal matters
summary: The UN Fund for Loss and Damage made its first grant, to flood-hit Nepal; the Indian Express says payouts must be faster and the Fund reformed.
evolution: Fund for Loss and Damage created at COP27, after a nearly three-decade campaign by vulnerable nations.
Fund operationalised.
First grant earmarked, to Nepal; developed countries insisted it is an exception, not a precedent.
COP31 begins in Antalya, Turkey, with compensation on the agenda.
